model_card.purpose: Institution-level failure early warning over the vetted Indian lender universe: corpus-calibrated PD term structure (discrete-time hazard, Shumway 2001, prior-corrected per King-Zeng 2001), distance to RBI PCA/SAF action zones, liability-side fragility, pre-registered forensic screen, and a Merton naive-DD market layer (Bharath-Shumway 2008) for listed names — fused by a PUBLISHED watchlist rule, never a hidden blend.
model_card.intended_use: Decision support for lender risk/treasury teams monitoring bank, SFB, UCB, NBFC, MFI and HFC counterparties and investments.
model_card.out_of_scope_use: Not a credit rating, not an automated action, not a solvency certification; PD levels inherit the documented tau base-rate judgment and a ~48-institution corpus.
assumptions: population 24m failure base rate ~0.5% (King-Zeng prior correction; sensitivity published in the validation payload)
constant hazard beyond the fitted 24m window (same survival scaling as the ECL engine)
Merton default barrier = disclosed deposits + borrowings (other liabilities not in the dossier schema; understatement disclosed per reading)
limitations: ~10 honest failure events ex-fraud: CIs are wide and published; the hazard model calibrates the validated disclosure score rather than replacing it
fraud-masked failures are invisible to every reported-number engine here; the forensic screen is the only lens pointed at them and it is deliberately conservative
unlisted institutions have no market layer; coverage stated per row
annual-only filers move the radar once a year — freshness is shown, not hidden
